rows.grounds: maṇi+saṅkhyaka; equal in number to beads

items.question: How many practitioners should be fed in connection with the rosary?
premises: Practitioners are to be fed.
Their number should match the beads.
items.inference: The ritual feeding should include practitioners equal in number to the rosary beads.
items.plain_english: One should also feed practitioners equal in number to the beads.

items.question: With which prepared rosary should mantra recitation be performed?
premises: A rosary is made with thread.
Recitation should be done with that rosary.
items.inference: Mantra recitation should be performed using the thread-made rosary.
items.plain_english: One should recite with that rosary which has been made on a thread.

items.question: In what concealed manner should the rosary be employed during recitation?
premises: The rosary should be employed for recitation.
Recitation should be done while it is concealed.
items.inference: One should use the rosary for recitation in a concealed manner.
uncertainties: The exact method of concealment is not specified.
items.plain_english: One should employ it and recite, but in such a way that it remains concealed.

items.question: What physical contacts and motions are forbidden when handling the rosary thread?
premises: The index finger must not touch the thread.
The thread must not be shaken or swung.
items.inference: Handling the rosary requires avoiding index-finger contact and agitating motions.
items.plain_english: One should not touch the thread with the index finger, nor shake it, nor swing it.

items.question: What contact must the thumb avoid while moving the rosary beads?
premises: The thumb moves the beads.
The thumb must not touch another bead.
items.inference: While moving beads, the thumb should contact only the intended bead.
items.plain_english: While moving the beads, the thumb should not touch any other bead.

items.question: What audible disturbance of the beads must be avoided during recitation?
premises: Beads can be made to clash.
Causing them to clash is prohibited.
items.inference: The practitioner must avoid making the beads strike against each other.
items.plain_english: But one should not cause the beads to clash together.

rows.grounds: second member of compound; occurrence of disease

items.question: What harmful consequences arise if a rosary bead breaks during use?
premises: A bead may break.
Breaking leads to hostility and disease.
items.inference: A broken bead is said to bring hostility and the arising of disease.
items.plain_english: If a bead breaks, hostility and the arising of disease result.

items.question: What alternative method of recitation uses the fingers as a rosary?
premises: Recitation can be done with finger rosaries.
This method is given a specific designation.
items.inference: One may perform recitation using the fingers as a rosary.
uncertainties: The specific name is stated in the following verse.
items.plain_english: Or one should perform recitation with the fingers as a rosary; that is what is called so.

rows.grounds: mūla+paryanta; extending from base to tip
kara+mālā; rosary formed by the hand

items.question: How is the hand-rosary defined in terms of its extent on the fingers?
premises: The hand can serve as a rosary.
It extends from base to end.
items.inference: The hand-rosary is defined as extending from the base to the end of the fingers.
items.plain_english: The hand-rosary is declared to extend from the base to the end.

items.question: From which finger base and in what order should the hand-rosary counting proceed?
premises: Counting begins at the ring-finger base.
It proceeds in sequence including the little finger.
items.inference: The hand-rosary count starts from the base of the ring finger and proceeds in order.
uncertainties: The full sequence of fingers is continued in the next verse.
items.plain_english: And starting from the base of the ring finger, proceeding in order to the little finger.

items.question: Which finger joint should be designated as the meru in the hand-rosary?
premises: A meru must be designated in the hand-rosary.
The first joint of the middle or ring finger serves this role.
items.inference: The first joint of the middle or ring finger should be designated as the meru.
items.plain_english: One should designate the first joint of the middle or ring finger as the meru.

rows.grounds: second member of compound; regulated procedure

items.question: How is the regulated method of finger recitation regarded in this teaching?
premises: A restraining method has been described.
It is declared and accepted as such.
items.inference: The described procedure is regarded as the proper regulated method.
items.plain_english: Thus the regulated method has been declared and is so regarded.

items.question: What authoritative position is taken regarding finger recitation versus other methods?
premises: Finger recitation has been declared.
No other method is accepted by the speaker.
items.inference: The speaker affirms finger recitation and rejects any other method as their own view.
items.plain_english: This is declared as finger recitation, and no other method is accepted by me.

items.question: What interruption must never occur during the time of recitation?
premises: Recitation has a designated time.
Separation or interruption must never happen then.
items.inference: One should never interrupt or disengage during the time of recitation.
items.plain_english: One should never break off at the time of recitation.

items.question: How should a qualified practitioner position the palm during recitation?
premises: The practitioner is qualified.
The palm should be slightly contracted.
items.inference: A qualified practitioner should keep the palm slightly contracted.
items.plain_english: A qualified person should slightly contract the palm.

items.question: Which mental faults and physical acts must be avoided during recitation practice?
premises: Jealousy, desire, and hatred are to be avoided.
Striking is also to be avoided.
items.inference: The practitioner must avoid jealousy, desire, hatred, and striking.
items.plain_english: One should avoid jealousy, desire, hatred, and striking.

rows.grounds: vibhītaka+karañja; two trees whose shade is avoided

items.question: Which sounds, substances, and specific tree-shades must be avoided during recitation?
premises: Musical instruments and honey are to be avoided.
The shade of vibhītaka and karañja trees is to be avoided.
items.inference: The practitioner must avoid musical instruments, honey, and the shade of vibhītaka and karañja.
items.plain_english: One should avoid musical instruments, honey, and the shade of the vibhītaka and karañja trees.

items.question: What transition marks the shift from prohibitions to required duties for the wise practitioner?
premises: The wise one should avoid certain things.
The duties to be performed are now to be heard.
items.inference: After listing prohibitions, the teaching turns to the duties the wise practitioner must hear and perform.
items.plain_english: The wise one should avoid these; now hear from me what must be done.

rows.grounds: second member of compound; forms of silence

items.question: What observances of silence and social avoidance are required as duties?
premises: Scriptural silence is required.
Association with others must be avoided.
items.inference: The practitioner must observe scriptural silence and avoid association with others.
items.plain_english: One must observe scriptural silence and avoid association with others.

rows.grounds: second member of compound; invitation to eat

items.question: What duties toward the teacher and food invitations must be observed?
premises: Worship of the teacher's feet is required.
Proper conduct regarding food invitations is required.
items.inference: The practitioner must worship the teacher's feet and observe proper conduct in food invitations.
uncertainties: The exact obligation in food invitation is contextually implied.
items.plain_english: One must worship the teacher's feet and respond properly to invitations for food.

items.question: Which ritual obligations of offerings and libations must be maintained?
premises: The five offerings are required.
Libation is also required.
items.inference: The practitioner must perform the five offerings and libation.
items.plain_english: The five offerings and libation must indeed be performed.

items.question: What corrective utterance must follow any accidental spoken sound during practice?
premises: A sound may be uttered once accidentally.
The praṇava should be uttered in response.
items.inference: If any sound is uttered, one should immediately utter the praṇava.
items.plain_english: If any sound is uttered even once, one should utter the praṇava.

items.question: What preparatory bodily ritual must precede mantra recitation?
premises: The limbs must be ritually placed.
Recitation follows that placement.
items.inference: One must necessarily perform placement on the limbs and then recite.
items.plain_english: One must necessarily place the mantras on the limbs and then recite.

items.question: What alternative devotional focus on Viṣṇu is permitted during recitation?
premises: One may recite a Vaiṣṇava mantra.
Alternatively one may remember Hari.
items.inference: The practitioner may either recite a Vaiṣṇava mantra or remember Hari.
items.plain_english: One should recite a Vaiṣṇava mantra or remember Hari.
